title: Sea surface temperature anomaly, worldwide, 2024 to 2026
summary: Twenty-four maps of the whole ocean, 38 days apart from May 2024 to October 2026, showing how much warmer or cooler the sea surface is than normal.
description: Sea surface temperature anomaly from NASA's MUR analysis (JPL PO DAAC), as drawn by NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio: blue where the sea is cooler than normal, white where it is near normal, and red where it is warmer, on a scale from minus 4 to plus 4 degrees Celsius. The map is flat, the whole world, with land and the polar ice in grey, which the app reads as no data. The original is a daily animation; this data set keeps one map every 38 days. The numbers are read from the colours of the maps, so they are about, not exact.

source.name: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio, Sea Surface Temperature (SST) Anomaly - Near Real Time (MUR SST, JPL PO DAAC)
source.credit: NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio. Visualizer: Kel Elkins (USRA). Scientist: Atousa Saberi (NASA/GSFC). Data: MUR SST (Multi-scale Ultra-high Resolution Sea Surface Temperature Analysis), JPL PO DAAC.

regions.name: The whole ocean
regions.description: The whole map, from pole to pole. Land and the polar ice are grey and count as no data.
